correctness.rationale: Uniform weak compositions yield exact one- and two-part marked stars-and-bars probabilities and a positive normalized cross-moment R for 1<=r<s, r+s<=n, k>=2. For k>2, the logarithmic derivative has sign 2-(s+1)T(k), with T a strictly increasing sum of x/(x+A_j)*(x-2)/(x+B_j), A_j>0 and B_j>=-2. At n=r+s it decreases throughout (the limit at 2 gives equality at the derivative endpoint), otherwise R rises once and falls once; its large-k limit (n-r)_s/(n)_s<1 yields one finite consecutive positive covariance band. Direct separate weak-composition enumeration and exact fractions reproduced n=10,r=1,s=6: k=2..7 ratios 0,22/25,26/25,26/25,1,20/21. This is an all-n,r,s proof; finite checks corroborate only bounded examples.

Related published SCOPE findings concern iid occupancy richness-versus-count and a uniform-composition maximum, not this two-frequency covariance under growing k.

value.rationale: Pairwise covariance of two abundance frequency classes is a natural statistic for species occupancy under Dirichlet-multinomial sampling. An exact one-band sign law prevents multiple correlations changing sign as category count increases and the explicit two-reversal witness demonstrates content beyond routine moment computation. It is an all-parameter structural shape theorem with a potentially useful parameter threshold, not merely one small experiment.

limitations: Prior general mixed-factorial moment formulas may encode an unnoticed equivalent rational sign inequality; no exhaustive historical priority certification.
Unequal Dirichlet parameters, repeated frequencies, or covariance magnitude unimodality are not covered.
